title: IBKR-scanner breadth snapshot concurrent-insert fix — non-blocking finding from PR #283's round-2 review
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's round-2 review of PR #283 (backend-market-breadth-indicators-followups-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges. Concerns the regression test added to fix round-1's raw-exception-leak finding.

checklist.step: `test_operational_error_with_no_same_key_winner_returns_503` (backend/tests/integration/test_ibkr_breadth.py:358-390) only asserts `"nh" in response.json()["detail"]`, so it does not actually guard against the exact regression the round-2 fix addressed (the raw SQLAlchemy exception -- interpolated SQL statement, bound parameters, and a sqlalche.me docs link -- leaking into the client-facing 503 `detail` at backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py:380-386). If a future edit re-adds `({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})` (or any other raw-exception interpolation) to that `HTTPException`'s `detail`, this test would still pass unchanged since `"nh"` remains present in the string -- the leak regression would ship silently with green CI. Worth strengthening the assertion to also check the exception-derived text is absent, e.g. `assert "SQL" not in response.json()["detail"]` and/or `assert "database is locked" not in response.json()["detail"]`, so the test actually fails if the interpolation is reintroduced.

decisions.decision: Strengthened `test_operational_error_with_no_same_key_winner_returns_503` to assert the full expected `detail` string exactly (`"Transient write conflict recording breadth snapshot for series_key='nh'; retry."`), plus separate negative assertions that known leak-indicator substrings (`OperationalError`, `database is locked`, `INSERT`, `sqlalche.me`) are absent from `detail`.
decisions.rationale: An exact-match assertion is the strongest guard against the round-1 leak regression (raw exception text re-interpolated into the client-facing detail) reappearing, since any such interpolation changes the string and fails the equality check immediately. The extra explicit substring-absence assertions were kept alongside it (rather than relying on exact-match alone) because they self-document exactly which leaked tokens this test exists to catch, matching the task's own suggested approach; considered using substring-absence checks only (no exact match), but rejected that since a still-loose substring set risks missing some other exception-derived fragment that happens not to match the chosen substrings, whereas pinning the full literal string can't miss any change to it.
